chap-web-07.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Explain the CSS Box Model (content, padding, border, margin) and describe why box-sizing: border-box simplifies web layouts.
chap-web-07.model_answer: The CSS Box Model defines element spacing. Content is the core area, padding is inner spacing, border wraps padding, and margin provides outer separation. It converts web pages into desktop apps

chap-web-10.question_text: What is the Mobile-First CSS design strategy?

Mobile-first design builds base CSS for mobile screens, using @media (min-width: ...) breakpoints to adjust layouts for tablets and desktops. Fluid units like rem and percentages maintain proportional scaling.

chap-js-07.question_text: What does e.preventDefault() do inside a form submit event handler?

options.text: Prevents the default browser page reload on form submission

chap-js-07.explanation: preventDefault stops default browser behaviors like form submission reloads or link clicks.

chap-js-07.question_text: In an event listener function (e) => { ... }, what does e.target refer to?

options.text: The specific DOM element that triggered the event

chap-js-07.explanation: e.target references the exact DOM element where the event originated.

chap-js-07.question_text: Which event type fires continuously as a user types into an <input> field?
chap-js-07.explanation: The 'input' event fires immediately whenever the input value changes.

chap-js-07.question_text: What is Event Delegation in DOM programming?

options.text: Deleting all event listeners on page unload
Attaching a single event listener to a parent container to handle events on multiple current or future child elements
Delegating JavaScript execution to a Web Worker

chap-js-07.explanation: Event delegation leverages event bubbling to manage listeners efficiently on parent elements.

chap-js-07.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Discuss event-driven programming in JS, addEventListener syntax, e.preventDefault(), and e.target usage.
chap-js-07.model_answer: Event-driven programming reacts to user actions. element.addEventListener('event', handler) listens for events like click, submit, and input. Inside handlers, e.target identifies the clicked element, and e.preventDefault() halts default browser actions like form reloads.
chap-js-07.explanation: Review the model answer to verify understanding of DOM event handling and prevention.

chap-js-08.question_text: What does it mean for JavaScript execution to be Asynchronous?

options.text: Long-running tasks execute in the background without freezing or blocking the main thread
JavaScript requires two CPUs to run
Functions execute strictly line by line without stopping

chap-js-08.explanation: Asynchronous code delegates network or timer tasks to background event loops.

chap-js-08.question_text: What are the three possible states of a JavaScript Promise?
chap-js-08.explanation: A Promise starts pending, then transitions to fulfilled (successful) or rejected (error).

chap-js-08.question_text: How do you pause execution inside an async function until a Promise settles?
chap-js-08.explanation: await pauses async function execution until the promise settles, returning its result.

chap-js-08.question_text: What is the correct syntax to extract JSON data from a fetch() HTTP response?
chap-js-08.explanation: response.json() returns a Promise resolving to parsed JSON data.

chap-js-08.question_text: Which block structure catches network errors during async/await fetch operations?
chap-js-08.explanation: try...catch blocks intercept exceptions thrown during asynchronous execution.

chap-js-08.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Explain asynchronous JS, Promises, async/await, and fetching remote API data using try/catch error handling.
chap-js-08.model_answer: Asynchronous JS handles background operations without blocking the main thread. Promises manage pending async states. async/await provides clean syntax where await pauses execution until a promise resolves. fetch() calls remote APIs, and try/catch blocks catch network or parsing errors.
chap-js-08.explanation: Review the model answer to verify understanding of async/await, fetch(), and error handling.

chap-js-09.question_text: What does the spread operator (...) do when applied to an array [...items, 99]?

options.text: Expands the elements of the items array into individual elements in a new array
Sorts the array in reverse order
Converts the array to a string

chap-js-09.explanation: The spread operator (...) unpacks iterable elements into individual positions.

chap-js-09.question_text: How does optional chaining (user?.profile?.avatar) prevent runtime crashes?

options.text: It returns undefined short-circuiting if any intermediate property is null or undefined, avoiding TypeErrors
It converts null into empty strings

chap-js-09.explanation: Optional chaining (?.) safely evaluates nested properties without throwing errors on nullish references.

chap-js-09.question_text: When does the nullish coalescing operator (val ?? 'Default') evaluate to 'Default'?

options.text: When val is false, 0, or empty string
ONLY when val is null or undefined

chap-js-09.explanation: Unlike ||, ?? only triggers fallback values when the target is null or undefined.

chap-js-09.question_text: How do you import a named export calculateXP from a module file './utils.js'?
chap-js-09.explanation: ES Module syntax uses import { name } from 'path'.

chap-js-09.question_text: What are Rest Parameters in function signatures like function total(...nums)?

options.text: Gathering all remaining function arguments into a single array parameter

chap-js-09.explanation: Rest parameters (...name) collect arbitrary function arguments into an array.

chap-js-09.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Detail modern ES6+ JS features including spread/rest operators, optional chaining (?.), nullish coalescing (??), and module imports.
chap-js-09.model_answer: Modern ES6+ features streamline code. Spread (...) expands arrays/objects, while rest parameters collect function arguments into arrays. Optional chaining (?.) prevents crashes on nullish nested references, nullish coalescing (??) fallbacks only on null/undefined, and ES Modules use import/export syntax.
chap-js-09.explanation: Review the model answer to verify understanding of modern ES6+ features.

chap-js-10.question_text: Which browser API method saves a key-value string pair across page reloads?
chap-js-10.explanation: localStorage.setItem persists data across browser reloads and tab closures.

chap-js-10.question_text: How do you store a complex JavaScript object in localStorage?

options.text: Pass the object directly into setItem
Convert it to a string using JSON.stringify(obj) before saving with setItem

chap-js-10.explanation: localStorage only stores strings, requiring JSON.stringify for objects.

chap-js-10.question_text: How do you retrieve and restore a saved object from localStorage?
chap-js-10.explanation: getItem retrieves the string, and JSON.parse reconstructs the original object.

chap-js-10.question_text: How long does data saved in localStorage persist?

options.text: Only until the browser tab is closed
Indefinitely until explicitly removed via code or cleared by the user

chap-js-10.explanation: Unlike sessionStorage, localStorage has no expiration time.

chap-js-10.question_text: Which method removes a specific key from localStorage?
chap-js-10.explanation: removeItem('key') deletes the specified key-value pair.

chap-js-10.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Explain state management in JS web apps, persistent storage using localStorage, and JSON object serialization.
chap-js-10.model_answer: State management tracks application data. localStorage persists data across sessions. Objects are serialized to strings with JSON.stringify before saving via localStorage.setItem, and restored using JSON.parse on localStorage.getItem.
chap-js-10.explanation: Review the model answer to verify understanding of localStorage and state persistence.

chap-cq-01.question_text: What is a computer program at its most fundamental level?

options.text: A step-by-step list of clear instructions a computer executes
A physical hammer inside the monitor
A magical spell with no rules

chap-cq-01.explanation: A computer program is a precise, ordered sequence of instructions that a computer carries out.

chap-cq-01.question_text: Why does instruction order matter when programming a robot?

options.text: It does not matter, computers guess what you want
Computers execute commands in the exact sequence given, so wrong order causes failure

chap-cq-01.explanation: Computers follow instructions sequentially from top to bottom. Order is critical.

chap-cq-01.question_text: What is a "bug" in software engineering?

options.text: A real insect trapped in the screen
An error, mistake, or unexpected flaw in code that causes wrong behavior
A bonus reward given to fast typists

chap-cq-01.explanation: A bug is an error in code that prevents a program from functioning correctly.

chap-cq-01.question_text: What is the process of finding and fixing mistakes in code called?
chap-cq-01.explanation: Debugging is the systematic process of locating and resolving errors in software.

chap-cq-01.question_text: What will be printed to the console by this code?

options.text: All three lines in top-to-bottom sequence

chap-cq-01.explanation: Console statements execute sequentially in the order written.

chap-cq-01.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Explain what an algorithm is in your own words, and give one real-world example of following sequential instructions.
chap-cq-01.model_answer: An algorithm is a step-by-step sequence of instructions designed to solve a problem or complete a task. A real-world example is a baking recipe or brushing your teeth, where each step must happen in order.
chap-cq-01.explanation: Algorithms require precise sequential logic to reach the desired outcome.

chap-cq-02.question_text: What is a variable in programming?

options.text: A named storage container that holds data in computer memory
A key on the keyboard that never changes
The speed of your internet connection

chap-cq-02.explanation: Variables act like labeled boxes in memory that store values you can use and update.

chap-cq-02.question_text: Which keyword in JavaScript declares a variable whose value can be changed later?
chap-cq-02.explanation: The let keyword declares a mutable variable in JavaScript.

chap-cq-02.question_text: What does the single equals sign (=) mean in programming?

options.text: Assignment: put the value on the right into the variable on the left
Comparison: check if both sides are identical

chap-cq-02.explanation: = is the assignment operator that assigns a value into a variable.

chap-cq-02.question_text: What will be printed after running this code?
chap-cq-02.explanation: 100 minus 30 results in 70 being stored in energy.

chap-cq-02.question_text: Which variable name follows standard camelCase conventions?
chap-cq-02.explanation: camelCase starts lowercase and capitalizes each subsequent word without spaces.

chap-cq-02.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: Why do programmers use variables instead of hard-coding raw numbers everywhere in their code? Give an example.
chap-cq-02.model_answer: Variables give meaningful names to data, make code easy to read, and allow values like player health or score to update dynamically without changing code in multiple places.
chap-cq-02.explanation: Variables provide readability, reusability, and dynamic state management.

chap-cq-03.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 3: Speaking in Code: Words & Numbers?

options.text: Numbers do math while Strings are text wrapped in quotes
Numbers must be wrapped in quotes

chap-cq-03.explanation: Strings represent text inside quotes; numbers represent numeric values for math.

chap-cq-03.question_text: What symbol is used to concatenate (glue) two strings together?
chap-cq-03.explanation: + combines strings into a single sentence.

chap-cq-03.question_text: What will be printed by this code snippet?
chap-cq-03.explanation: The space string between first and second separates the two words.

chap-cq-03.question_text: What data type is the value 42 (without quotes)?
What happens if you add "5" + "5" (both in quotes)?
chap-cq-03.explanation: String concatenation glues characters together: "5" + "5" becomes "55".

chap-cq-03.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Speaking in Code: Words & Numbers works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-03.model_answer: Strings represent text wrapped in quotes, while Numbers represent numeric values used for math. Adding numbers calculates a sum, but adding strings concatenates them together into one longer text.
chap-cq-03.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Speaking in Code: Words & Numbers.

chap-cq-04.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 4: The Fork in the Road: Making Decisions?

options.text: If-else statements let programs make choices based on true/false conditions
Decisions can only happen once per day

chap-cq-04.explanation: Conditional statements allow programs to take different paths depending on evaluated conditions.

chap-cq-04.question_text: What are the only two possible values of a Boolean data type?
chap-cq-04.explanation: Booleans represent binary truth values: true or false.

chap-cq-04.question_text: What will this code print when energy is 80?
chap-cq-04.explanation: 80 is greater than 50, so the if block executes.

chap-cq-04.question_text: What operator checks if two values are equal in modern JavaScript?
chap-cq-04.explanation: === checks for strict equality of value and type.

chap-cq-04.question_text: When does the "else" branch of an if-else statement run?

options.text: Only when the if condition evaluates to false

chap-cq-04.explanation: The else block is the fallback that runs when the condition is false.

chap-cq-04.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how The Fork in the Road: Making Decisions works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-04.model_answer: If-else statements allow computers to make decisions dynamically. A condition is evaluated: if true, the code inside the if block runs; otherwise, the alternative code in the else block executes.
chap-cq-04.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of The Fork in the Road: Making Decisions.

chap-cq-05.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 5: Loop-de-Loop: The Power of Repetition?

options.text: Loops repeat code instructions multiple times without duplicating lines

chap-cq-05.question_text: What loop is best when you know in advance exactly how many times to repeat?
chap-cq-05.explanation: A for loop has a built-in counter ideal for fixed repetitions.

chap-cq-05.question_text: How many times will this loop execute?
chap-cq-05.explanation: The loop runs for i = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, which is 5 iterations.

chap-cq-05.question_text: What danger occurs if a while loop condition never becomes false?

options.text: An infinite loop that freezes the program

chap-cq-05.explanation: Without an exit condition, while loops run forever and freeze execution.

chap-cq-05.question_text: What does "i++" do in a loop?

options.text: Increments the counter variable i by 1

chap-cq-05.explanation: i++ is shorthand for i = i + 1.

chap-cq-05.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Loop-de-Loop: The Power of Repetition works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-05.model_answer: Loops repeat a block of code multiple times based on a counter or condition. They save time and prevent repetitive code, making it easy to perform tasks like counting, animations, or processing items.
chap-cq-05.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Loop-de-Loop: The Power of Repetition.

chap-cq-06.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 6: Magic Backpacks: Lists and Arrays?

options.text: Arrays store multiple items in an indexed list inside square brackets []
Arrays only hold one single letter

chap-cq-06.explanation: Arrays are ordered collections capable of storing multiple elements.

chap-cq-06.question_text: What is the index number of the very FIRST item in an array?
chap-cq-06.explanation: Computers start counting array items at index 0.

chap-cq-06.question_text: What item will be logged by this array lookup?
chap-cq-06.explanation: Index 0 is Mars; index 1 is Jupiter.

chap-cq-06.question_text: What array property tells you how many items are inside the list?
chap-cq-06.explanation: .length returns the total count of elements in an array.

chap-cq-06.question_text: Which array method adds a new item to the very end of a list?
chap-cq-06.explanation: .push() appends new elements to the end of an array.

chap-cq-06.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Magic Backpacks: Lists and Arrays works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-06.model_answer: An array is an ordered collection that stores multiple items under a single variable name using square brackets. Items are accessed using zero-based index numbers, with the first item at index 0.
chap-cq-06.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Magic Backpacks: Lists and Arrays.

chap-cq-07.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 7: Robot Superpowers: Functions & Reusability?

options.text: Functions package reusable code blocks that can be called whenever needed
Functions only run once and self-destruct

chap-cq-07.explanation: Functions provide modularity, reusability, and clean abstraction.

chap-cq-07.question_text: What keyword defines a function in JavaScript?
chap-cq-07.explanation: The function keyword declares a reusable function.

chap-cq-07.question_text: What will be printed when calculateEnergy(10, 5) is called?
What keyword sends a result back from a function to the caller?
chap-cq-07.explanation: return yields a value back from the function execution.

chap-cq-07.question_text: What are the variables passed into a function inside parentheses called?
chap-cq-07.explanation: Parameters define the expected inputs inside function definitions.

chap-cq-07.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Robot Superpowers: Functions & Reusability works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-07.model_answer: A function is a named block of code that performs a specific task. It can accept parameters as inputs and use the return keyword to output a result, allowing code to be reused without duplication.
chap-cq-07.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Robot Superpowers: Functions & Reusability.

chap-cq-08.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 8: Bug Hunters: Debugging Detective Lab?

options.text: Debugging means finding syntax errors, logic flaws, and runtime exceptions

chap-cq-08.explanation: Debugging identifies and fixes errors in software.

chap-cq-08.question_text: What kind of error happens when you forget a closing bracket or quote?
chap-cq-08.explanation: Syntax errors break the grammar rules of the programming language.

chap-cq-08.question_text: What is the bug in this code snippet?

options.text: Missing closing single quote on the string

chap-cq-08.explanation: The string literal is missing its closing quotation mark.

chap-cq-08.question_text: What tool helps programmers inspect values and see where errors occur?

options.text: A magnifying glass on the monitor

chap-cq-08.explanation: console.log outputs diagnostic state to the developer console.

options.text: The code runs without crashing, but produces the wrong mathematical result
The computer runs out of battery

chap-cq-08.explanation: Logic errors happen when code syntax is valid but the algorithmic logic is wrong.

chap-cq-08.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Bug Hunters: Debugging Detective Lab works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-08.model_answer: Debugging is the detective work of finding and fixing mistakes in code. Syntax errors break language grammar, while logic errors produce wrong results. Programmers use console.log and careful testing to resolve bugs.
chap-cq-08.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Bug Hunters: Debugging Detective Lab.

chap-cq-09.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 9: Interactive Worlds: Responding to Events?

options.text: Event-driven programming triggers code in response to user actions like clicks and keys
Events only happen in video games

chap-cq-09.explanation: Events listen for user interactions and execute handler functions.

chap-cq-09.question_text: Which event triggers when a student presses a key on their keyboard?
chap-cq-09.explanation: keydown triggers as soon as any key is pressed.

chap-cq-09.question_text: What will happen when the button is clicked in this code?

options.text: "Shields deployed!" is logged to the console

chap-cq-09.explanation: The click event listener runs the callback function.

chap-cq-09.question_text: What method registers an event listener on an interactive element?
chap-cq-09.explanation: addEventListener is the standard DOM method to bind events.

chap-cq-09.question_text: Why is event-driven programming important for games and apps?

options.text: It makes programs interactive and responsive to player controls in real time
It makes text black and white

chap-cq-09.explanation: Events enable responsive, real-time interactivity for buttons and keys.

chap-cq-09.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Interactive Worlds: Responding to Events works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-09.model_answer: Event-driven programming lets code respond to user actions like clicking buttons or pressing keys. An event listener waits for an action to happen, then immediately runs a handler function to update the app.
chap-cq-09.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Interactive Worlds: Responding to Events.

chap-cq-10.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 10: Capstone Project: Space Station Simulator?

options.text: A full software project integrates variables, conditionals, loops, functions, and events into a unified system
A project only needs one line of code
Projects cannot have more than two variables
A capstone is an exam with zero code

chap-cq-10.explanation: The capstone brings together all foundational computer science concepts.

chap-cq-10.question_text: What is state in an interactive application?

options.text: The current values of all variables tracking player score, health, and status
The country where the server is located

chap-cq-10.explanation: State represents the collective dynamic data in an app at any given moment.

chap-cq-10.question_text: What is the role of a main game loop in a simulation?

options.text: To update status, check conditions, and render changes repeatedly

chap-cq-10.explanation: The game loop continuously updates simulation logic and renders output.

chap-cq-10.question_text: Why is modular design with helper functions good practice in large projects?

options.text: It keeps code organized, readable, and easy to test and maintain
It makes files larger on purpose

chap-cq-10.explanation: Modular functions break complex programs into manageable pieces.

chap-cq-10.question_text: What makes a program user-friendly and engaging?

options.text: Clear feedback, responsive controls, intuitive rules, and clean visual cues

chap-cq-10.explanation: Good user experience combines clarity, responsiveness, and aesthetic polish.

chap-cq-10.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Capstone Project: Space Station Simulator works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-cq-10.model_answer: The Space Station Simulator synthesizes all core programming concepts: variables track station resources, conditionals enforce safety limits, loops calculate telemetry, functions organize subsystems, and events handle player commands.
chap-cq-10.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Capstone Project: Space Station Simulator.

chap-gm-01.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 1: What Makes a Game Tick??

options.text: The Game Loop continuously processes input, updates game state, and renders graphics
Games only run once per day

chap-gm-01.explanation: The game loop is the continuous heartbeat of all video games.

options.text: Frames Per Second: how many times the screen updates each second

chap-gm-01.explanation: FPS measures graphic rendering frequency; 60 FPS is standard for smooth gameplay.

chap-gm-01.question_text: What will be the player score after collecting 3 stars worth 10 points each?
What are the 3 core phases of every game loop cycle?

options.text: 1. Handle Input, 2. Update Physics/State, 3. Draw/Render Graphics

chap-gm-01.explanation: Input, Update, and Render form the triad of game loops.

chap-gm-01.question_text: What tracks whether the player is currently playing, paused, or game-over?
chap-gm-01.explanation: State variables control active gameplay screens and mechanics.

chap-gm-01.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how What Makes a Game Tick? works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-01.model_answer: A game loop is the core engine of a video game. It runs up to 60 times per second, continuously reading player inputs, updating coordinates and physics, and rendering graphics onto the canvas.
chap-gm-01.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of What Makes a Game Tick?.

chap-gm-02.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 2: The 2D Grid: X & Y Coordinates?

options.text: X moves horizontally (left/right) and Y moves vertically (up/down)
X is color and Y is sound
X is volume and Y is score

chap-gm-02.explanation: The 2D Cartesian grid maps every pixel by (X, Y) positions.

chap-gm-02.question_text: In computer graphics (Canvas/HTML), where is the origin coordinate (0, 0)?

options.text: The TOP-LEFT corner of the canvas
The exact center of the screen

chap-gm-02.explanation: Screen coordinates start at (0, 0) in the top-left; Y increases as you go downwards.

chap-gm-02.question_text: If a spaceship moves right, what coordinate increases?
chap-gm-02.explanation: Increasing X translates an object to the right.

chap-gm-02.question_text: In screen coordinates, what happens to playerY when jumping UP?

options.text: playerY DECREASES because Y = 0 is at the top of the screen

chap-gm-02.explanation: Moving upward decreases the Y coordinate toward 0.

chap-gm-02.question_text: What coordinate marks the horizontal center of an 800-pixel wide canvas?
Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how The 2D Grid: X & Y Coordinates works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-02.model_answer: A 2D coordinate system uses X for horizontal positioning and Y for vertical positioning. In canvas programming, (0, 0) is at the top-left corner: moving right increases X, and moving down increases Y.
chap-gm-02.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of The 2D Grid: X & Y Coordinates.

chap-gm-03.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 3: Player Controls: Moving on Arrow Keys?

options.text: Event listeners capture Arrow or WASD keys to adjust player position coordinates
Arrow keys only work in Word

chap-gm-03.explanation: Key listeners translate button presses into positional velocity.

chap-gm-03.question_text: Which key code or key name is pressed to move a player to the left?
chap-gm-03.explanation: ArrowLeft and KeyA are standard leftward inputs.

chap-gm-03.question_text: What will happen when ArrowRight is pressed with speed = 5?

options.text: playerX increases by 5, moving the sprite rightward

chap-gm-03.explanation: Adding speed to playerX pushes the sprite to the right.

chap-gm-03.question_text: Why is it important to prevent a player from walking off the screen boundaries?

options.text: To keep the character visible and inside the active gameplay arena
To stop the computer from restarting

chap-gm-03.explanation: Clamping coordinates prevents characters from disappearing off-screen.

chap-gm-03.question_text: What function clamps a number between a minimum and maximum boundary?
chap-gm-03.explanation: Bounding using min and max restricts values within bounds.

chap-gm-03.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Player Controls: Moving on Arrow Keys works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-03.model_answer: Player movement is created by listening for keydown events. When an arrow key is detected, the program changes the player's X or Y coordinates by a speed amount, while clamping coordinates inside screen boundaries.
chap-gm-03.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Player Controls: Moving on Arrow Keys.

chap-gm-04.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 4: Collision Chaos: When Objects Touch!?

options.text: Collision detection calculates when two bounding boxes overlap in 2D space
Objects can pass through each other without math

chap-gm-04.explanation: AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) detects rectangular overlaps.

chap-gm-04.question_text: What does AABB stand for in game collision physics?
chap-gm-04.explanation: AABB is the standard bounding-box collision algorithm.

chap-gm-04.question_text: What happens when a player collides with a coin in a game?

options.text: Score increases by 100 and the coin is marked collected

chap-gm-04.explanation: Overlapping triggers reward points and collects the coin.

chap-gm-04.question_text: What happens when a player collides with an enemy or hazard?

options.text: Player health or lives decrease, or trigger a game-over screen

chap-gm-04.explanation: Hazard collisions reduce player health or restart levels.

chap-gm-04.question_text: How do you check if two horizontal lines overlap from x1 to x1+w1 and x2 to x2+w2?
chap-gm-04.explanation: This verifies mutual horizontal overlap between bounding boxes.

chap-gm-04.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Collision Chaos: When Objects Touch! works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-04.model_answer: Collision detection calculates whether the hitboxes of two game sprites overlap. If the player's bounding box touches a collectible, score increases; if it touches a hazard, player health decreases.
chap-gm-04.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Collision Chaos: When Objects Touch!.

chap-gm-05.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 5: Coin Collector: Scores, Timers & Sound FX?

options.text: A HUD (Heads-Up Display) displays real-time score, lives, and countdown timers

chap-gm-05.explanation: The HUD keeps players informed about their progress and status.

chap-gm-05.question_text: What JavaScript function executes a countdown every 1000 milliseconds (1 second)?
chap-gm-05.explanation: setInterval repeatedly calls a function at fixed time intervals.

chap-gm-05.question_text: What will happen when timeRemaining hits 0 in this game loop?

options.text: The game transitions to the GAME_OVER state
The timer starts counting up to 1000

chap-gm-05.explanation: Reaching 0 time ends the active play session.

chap-gm-05.question_text: How do sound effects enhance game design?

options.text: They provide auditory feedback for jumps, coin grabs, and collisions
They make the game file 1000x larger

chap-gm-05.explanation: Audio cues give players instant sensory satisfaction and clarity.

chap-gm-05.question_text: What does high score persistence achieve in arcade games?

options.text: It rewards player improvement and motivates replayability across sessions
It stops new players from trying

chap-gm-05.explanation: Saving high scores fuels friendly competition and mastery.

chap-gm-05.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Coin Collector: Scores, Timers & Sound FX works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-05.model_answer: A game HUD displays real-time statistics like score, remaining time, and lives. Combining visual counters with audio effects gives players immediate feedback, making games exciting and intuitive to play.
chap-gm-05.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Coin Collector: Scores, Timers & Sound FX.

chap-gm-06.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 6: Bouncing Physics: Gravity, Speed & Walls?

options.text: Velocity is speed with direction; gravity continuously adds downward velocity

chap-gm-06.explanation: Velocity dictates motion, while gravity exerts downward acceleration.

chap-gm-06.question_text: What happens to a ball's vertical velocity (vy) when it bounces off the floor?

options.text: vy flips direction: vy = -vy (multiplied by bounce damping)
vy doubles in the same direction

chap-gm-06.explanation: Reversing sign (negative) sends the velocity upward.

chap-gm-06.question_text: What happens to a character during a jump?
chap-gm-06.code:
velocityY = -12; // Initial upward burst
velocityY += gravity; // Gravity pulls down each frame

options.text: The character leaps upward, slows down, peaks, and falls back down
The character flies into space forever
The character burrows into the floor

chap-gm-06.explanation: Gravity decelerates the upward jump and accelerates downward fall.

chap-gm-06.question_text: What is friction or damping in video game physics?

options.text: A slight slowdown applied each frame so moving sprites gradually stop gliding

chap-gm-06.explanation: Damping simulates air resistance and ground friction.

chap-gm-06.question_text: What happens when a ball hits the right wall at canvas.width?
chap-gm-06.explanation: Reversing horizontal velocity bounces the ball back to the left.

chap-gm-06.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Bouncing Physics: Gravity, Speed & Walls works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-06.model_answer: Game physics uses velocity (speed and direction) to update coordinates each frame. Gravity adds a continuous downward force to vertical velocity. When hitting a boundary or floor, velocity reverses to create a realistic bounce.
chap-gm-06.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Bouncing Physics: Gravity, Speed & Walls.

chap-gm-07.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 7: Smart Enemies: Patrols & Chasers?

options.text: Enemy AI uses logic rules like patrolling back-and-forth or moving towards the player
Enemies are controlled by human players online only

chap-gm-07.explanation: Automated AI scripts create engaging gameplay challenges.

chap-gm-07.question_text: How does a patrol enemy turn around when hitting a patrol edge?
chap-gm-07.explanation: Inverting direction toggles between moving left and right.

chap-gm-07.question_text: How does a chaser enemy track the player's position?

options.text: The enemy steps towards the player's X coordinate
The enemy moves away from the player

chap-gm-07.explanation: Comparing X coordinates steers the enemy toward the player.

chap-gm-07.question_text: Why do good games make enemies predictable rather than impossibly fast?

options.text: So players can learn patterns, time their moves, and feel clever when winning

chap-gm-07.explanation: Predictable enemy patterns create fair, fun gameplay loops.

chap-gm-07.question_text: What happens when a player jumps directly on top of an enemy's head in classic platformers?

options.text: The enemy is defeated and the player bounces upward

chap-gm-07.explanation: Stomping enemies rewards skillful aerial positioning.

chap-gm-07.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Smart Enemies: Patrols & Chasers works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-07.model_answer: Enemy AI gives computer-controlled opponents lifelike behavior. Patrol enemies pace back and forth between boundaries, while chasers compare coordinates to track the player. Recognizable patterns allow players to dodge or defeat them.
chap-gm-07.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Smart Enemies: Patrols & Chasers.

chap-gm-08.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 8: Level Design: Spawning Platforms & Hazards?

options.text: Levels are structured using arrays of platform coordinates and obstacle locations
Levels are drawn randomly with no code
Every game can only have 1 platform

chap-gm-08.explanation: Storing level data in arrays makes stages modular and expandable.

chap-gm-08.question_text: How does a loop render 10 platforms stored in an array?

options.text: It iterates through the array and draws each platform at its (x, y, width, height)
It only draws the first one

chap-gm-08.explanation: Array iteration renders each platform in the stage.

options.text: The player safely lands on top of the platform and resets falling velocity

chap-gm-08.explanation: Aligning feet to the platform top creates solid ground.

chap-gm-08.question_text: What makes a video game level feel fun and well-paced?

options.text: Starting with easy mechanics, introducing new challenges gradually, and rewarding exploration
Making the first jump impossible to beat

chap-gm-08.explanation: Progressive difficulty curves keep players engaged and learning.

chap-gm-08.question_text: What is a death pit or bottom void in platformers?

options.text: Falling below canvas.height causes player defeat or respawn at checkpoint

chap-gm-08.explanation: Falling off the stage resets the player to a safe checkpoint.

chap-gm-08.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Level Design: Spawning Platforms & Hazards works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-08.model_answer: Level design structures game environments using arrays of platforms and hazards. Collision checks ensure players land cleanly on surfaces, while progressive difficulty introduces moving obstacles, spikes, and checkpoints.
chap-gm-08.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Level Design: Spawning Platforms & Hazards.

chap-gm-09.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 9: Animation Station: Sprite Frames & Particle FX?

options.text: Animation cycles through sprite frames over time, and particles create sparks or dust
Sprites are static photos that cannot move

chap-gm-09.explanation: Frame cycling creates the illusion of running, jumping, and celebrating.

chap-gm-09.question_text: What creates the illusion of running in a 2D game character?

options.text: Swapping between 4-8 running animation frame drawings rapidly in sequence

chap-gm-09.explanation: Frame flipping relies on persistence of vision to show motion.

chap-gm-09.question_text: What happens to particle effects (sparks, smoke) over their lifetime?

options.text: Particles burst outward, float, fade in opacity, and disappear when alpha <= 0

chap-gm-09.explanation: Particle systems simulate dynamic bursts that fade naturally.

chap-gm-09.question_text: What is "game juice" in game development?

options.text: Juicy visual polish like screen shake, particle bursts, and smooth squash & stretch animations

chap-gm-09.explanation: Juice refers to sensory embellishments that make games satisfying to play.

chap-gm-09.question_text: Why should expired particles (alpha <= 0) be removed from the particle array?

options.text: To free computer memory and maintain a high, smooth 60 FPS frame rate
Because computers can only hold 5 items

chap-gm-09.explanation: Garbage collecting dead particles prevents memory leaks and frame drops.

chap-gm-09.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Animation Station: Sprite Frames & Particle FX works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-09.model_answer: Animations bring games to life by cycling sprite frames in sequence to depict running and jumping. Particle effects create bursts of sparks and dust that disperse, fade, and clean up, adding satisfying visual polish.
chap-gm-09.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Animation Station: Sprite Frames & Particle FX.

chap-gm-10.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 10: Capstone Game: Star Collector Odyssey?

options.text: A full indie game integrates player controls, physics, animated sprites, enemy AI, and multi-stage levels
A game only needs a start button and nothing else

chap-gm-10.explanation: The capstone demonstrates mastery of complete game programming architecture.

chap-gm-10.question_text: What are the 3 primary screens of a polished game lifecycle?

options.text: Title Screen (Start) ➔ Active Gameplay Screen ➔ Victory / Game Over Screen
Black Screen ➔ White Screen ➔ Gray Screen

chap-gm-10.explanation: Title, Gameplay, and End screens form the classic game lifecycle.

chap-gm-10.question_text: What happens when a player collects all star relics and reaches the portal?

options.text: The game advances to the victory celebration screen

chap-gm-10.explanation: Satisfying victory conditions triggers game completion.

chap-gm-10.question_text: What is the most rewarding part of building your own video game from scratch?

options.text: Designing rules, seeing code come alive into playful interactive fun, and sharing it with friends!

chap-gm-10.explanation: Creating worlds and sharing interactive experiences is the joy of programming.

chap-gm-10.question_text: What badge did you earn by completing the Game Makers curriculum?

options.text: Certified Game Maker & Junior Game Developer 🏆

chap-gm-10.explanation: Graduating completes the full 10-chapter game developer track!

chap-gm-10.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Capstone Game: Star Collector Odyssey works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-gm-10.model_answer: Star Collector Odyssey unites all game development pillars: responsive player movement, realistic gravity and collision physics, patrol enemy AI, animated particle effects, a clear HUD, and distinct title, gameplay, and victory screens.
chap-gm-10.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Capstone Game: Star Collector Odyssey.

chap-we-01.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 1: The Magic Highway of the Internet?

options.text: The web connects clients (browsers asking for pages) to servers (computers hosting files)
Websites live inside the monitor glass
The internet is a single USB stick

chap-we-01.explanation: Clients send requests across the internet to servers, which respond with HTML and media.

chap-we-01.question_text: What is the primary role of a web browser like Chrome or Safari?

options.text: To download HTML/CSS text files and translate them into visual interactive pages

chap-we-01.explanation: Browsers parse code files into visual DOM trees on screen.

chap-we-01.question_text: What file extension is used for web documents?
What developer tool allows you to inspect the HTML and CSS of any website live?

options.text: Inspect Element / Developer Tools (F12 or Right Click)

chap-we-01.explanation: Inspect Element exposes the live DOM tree and active CSS styles.

options.text: The unique web address pointing to a specific page on a server

chap-we-01.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a web resource.

chap-we-01.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how The Magic Highway of the Internet works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-01.model_answer: The World Wide Web is a global network connecting clients and servers. When you enter a URL in a browser (client), an HTTP request travels across the internet to a server, which sends back HTML and CSS files to render on screen.
chap-we-01.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of The Magic Highway of the Internet.

chap-we-02.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 2: HTML — The Building Bricks?

options.text: HTML provides the structural skeleton of web pages using opening and closing tags
HTML is only for coloring buttons

chap-we-02.explanation: HTML tags wrap content to define headings, paragraphs, and semantic sections.

chap-we-02.question_text: What symbol distinguishes a closing HTML tag from an opening tag?
chap-we-02.explanation: Closing tags always contain a forward slash before the tag name.

chap-we-02.question_text: What heading tag produces the largest, primary title on a web page?
chap-we-02.explanation: <h1> is the top-level, largest semantic heading.

chap-we-02.question_text: Which tag creates a single line break without starting an entire new paragraph?
chap-we-02.explanation: inserts a single line break carriage return.

chap-we-02.question_text: What semantic tag makes text bold with strong importance for accessibility?
chap-we-02.explanation: <strong> renders bold text with semantic importance for screen readers.

chap-we-02.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how HTML — The Building Bricks works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-02.model_answer:
HTML provides the foundational structure of web pages. Elements use opening tags like

and closing tags like

to wrap content. Semantic tags like headings (h1-h6), paragraphs (p), and line breaks (br) organize information clearly.
chap-we-02.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of HTML — The Building Bricks.

chap-we-03.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 3: Adding Pictures to the Page?

options.text: The tag embeds photos using the src attribute and provides descriptions via alt text
Images must be black and white

chap-we-03.explanation: Images are embedded via self-closing tags with source paths.

chap-we-03.question_text: What attribute specifies the image file location or web URL?
chap-we-03.explanation: src stands for "source" and points to the image file.

chap-we-03.question_text: Why is the "alt" attribute essential on all image tags?

options.text: It describes the image for blind students using screen readers, and shows if images fail to load
It speeds up the computer fan
It deletes the image after 5 seconds

chap-we-03.explanation: Alt text ensures accessibility for screen readers and fallbacks.

chap-we-03.question_text: What attributes control the pixel dimensions of an image directly in HTML?
chap-we-03.explanation: width and height scale images in pixel dimensions.

chap-we-03.question_text: What happens if there is a spelling typo in an image filename inside the src attribute?

options.text: The browser displays a broken image icon and shows the alt text fallback

chap-we-03.explanation: Path typos cause 404 missing resource errors, displaying alt text.

chap-we-03.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Adding Pictures to the Page works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-03.model_answer: The tag embeds visual media into a webpage without a closing tag. The src attribute tells the browser where to find the picture, width and height control dimensions, and alt text describes the image for accessibility and screen readers.
chap-we-03.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Adding Pictures to the Page.

chap-we-04.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 4: Hyperlinks — The Web's Secret Portals?

options.text: The <a> anchor tag connects web pages across the world using href destination URLs
Hyperlinks can only link to the same computer
Links cannot be clicked with a mouse

chap-we-04.explanation: Hyperlinks are the interconnected bridges that define the World Wide Web.

chap-we-04.question_text: What attribute in an <a> tag defines where the link teleports the user?
chap-we-04.explanation: href (Hypertext Reference) specifies the link destination.

chap-we-04.question_text: What attribute makes a link open in a shiny new browser tab?
chap-we-04.explanation: target="_blank" tells browsers to launch the destination in a new tab.

chap-we-04.question_text: How do you make an image clickable like a button?

options.text: Wrap the tag inside an ... tag

Add a

tag inside the image

chap-we-04.explanation: Nesting an inside an turns the picture into a clickable link.

chap-we-04.question_text: What symbol is placed before an ID to create a jump link on the same page?
chap-we-04.explanation: #id scrolls the viewport directly to the matching element ID.

chap-we-04.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Hyperlinks — The Web's Secret Portals works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-04.model_answer: Hyperlinks use the <a> (anchor) tag to connect pages across the internet. The href attribute specifies the destination URL, while target="_blank" opens links in new tabs. Wrapping images in anchor tags transforms visuals into clickable portals.
chap-we-04.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Hyperlinks — The Web's Secret Portals.

chap-we-05.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 5: Organizing with Lists?

options.text: Lists organize items into bulleted (ul) or sequentially numbered (ol) collections using li tags
Lists are forbidden on web pages

chap-we-05.explanation: Lists structure content into clean bulleted or numbered formats.

chap-we-05.question_text: What tag creates an unordered bulleted list?
What tag wraps every individual item inside a list?
chap-we-05.explanation: <li> tags wrap list items inside both <ul> and <ol>.

chap-we-05.question_text: What tag creates an ordered list that automatically numbers items 1, 2, 3...?
chap-we-05.explanation: <ol> creates an ordered, sequentially numbered list.

chap-we-05.question_text: What semantic HTML element wraps navigation menus built with lists?
chap-we-05.explanation: <nav> is the dedicated semantic container for navigation links.

chap-we-05.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Organizing with Lists works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-05.model_answer: Lists organize content cleanly on the web. <ul> creates unordered bulleted lists, <ol> produces ordered numbered lists, and <li> encloses each item. Placing an unordered list inside a <nav> element forms the universal foundation for website navigation menus.
chap-we-05.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Organizing with Lists.

chap-we-06.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 6: Splashing Colors with CSS?

options.text: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) decorates HTML elements with colors, fonts, and backgrounds
CSS can only be written in black

chap-we-06.explanation: CSS is the presentation and styling language of the web.

chap-we-06.question_text: What attribute allows you to write CSS rules directly inside an HTML tag?
chap-we-06.explanation: The style attribute applies inline CSS directly to an element.

chap-we-06.question_text: What CSS property changes the text color of an element?
chap-we-06.explanation: color specifies the foreground text color.

chap-we-06.question_text: What CSS property changes the container background canvas fill?
chap-we-06.explanation: background-color fills the element container with solid color.

chap-we-06.question_text: What punctuation separates multiple CSS properties inside a style rule?
chap-we-06.explanation: Semicolons separate adjacent CSS property declarations.

chap-we-06.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Splashing Colors with CSS works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-06.model_answer: CSS controls the visual styling of a website. Using inline style attributes, developers can define color for text and background-color for container fills. Hex codes provide pinpoint color precision, and semicolons separate multiple CSS properties.
chap-we-06.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Splashing Colors with CSS.

chap-we-07.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 7: Fun with Fonts & Borders?

options.text: CSS controls typography with font-family and font-size, and frames containers with borders and border-radius
Fonts cannot be changed in browsers
Borders are only allowed in printed books

chap-we-07.explanation: Typography and border geometry establish visual hierarchy and personality.

chap-we-07.question_text: What CSS property rounds the sharp corners of buttons and cards?
chap-we-07.explanation: border-radius rounds the corners of rectangular boxes.

chap-we-07.question_text: What 3 values make up a complete border shorthand rule?
chap-we-07.explanation: Width, style, and color form the standard CSS border declaration.

chap-we-07.question_text: Which font-family category gives letters an authentic computer terminal look?
chap-we-07.explanation: monospace fonts give characters uniform equal width like code terminals.

chap-we-07.question_text: What unit of measurement is most commonly used for font-size in web design?
chap-we-07.explanation: px (pixels) is the standard digital screen measurement unit.

chap-we-07.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Fun with Fonts & Borders works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-07.model_answer: Typography and borders create visual polish in CSS. font-family selects typefaces (like sans-serif or monospace) while font-size scales text in pixels. The border property frames elements with width, style, and color, and border-radius softens sharp corners into modern rounded cards.
chap-we-07.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Fun with Fonts & Borders.

chap-we-08.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 8: Spacing Out: Margins & Padding?

options.text: The Box Model treats every element as a box with Content, Padding (inside), Border, and Margin (outside)
Elements on web pages are circles with no spacing
Spacing cannot be adjusted in CSS

chap-we-08.explanation: The Box Model is the foundational layout architecture of CSS.

chap-we-08.question_text: Which CSS property creates breathing room INSIDE a box, pushing text away from the border?
chap-we-08.explanation: Padding adds internal space between content and the border.

chap-we-08.question_text: Which CSS property creates separation OUTSIDE a box, pushing neighboring elements away?
chap-we-08.explanation: Margin creates external space around an element.

chap-we-08.question_text: What CSS rule centers a fixed-width container horizontally in the browser window?
chap-we-08.explanation: margin: 0 auto evenly distributes remaining horizontal space on both sides.

chap-we-08.question_text: What are the four layers of the CSS Box Model from the inside out?
chap-we-08.explanation: Content is at the center, surrounded by padding, then border, then margin.

chap-we-08.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Spacing Out: Margins & Padding works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-08.model_answer: The CSS Box Model governs how every element occupies space. Content sits at the center, surrounded by padding for internal breathing room. The border frames the perimeter, and margin creates external separation between neighboring elements.
chap-we-08.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Spacing Out: Margins & Padding.

chap-we-09.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 9: Connecting Multi-Page Websites?

options.text: Multi-page websites organize HTML files into folders and link them using relative paths and consistent navigation
A website can only ever have 1 single page
Relative links do not work in HTML

chap-we-09.explanation: Structuring pages with relative paths enables rich multi-page web applications.

chap-we-09.question_text: What is the universal default filename for the homepage of any website?
chap-we-09.explanation: Web servers automatically serve index.html as the root landing page.

chap-we-09.question_text: If photo.jpg is stored inside an "images" folder, what is the relative src path?
chap-we-09.explanation: images/photo.jpg references the file inside the images subfolder.

chap-we-09.question_text: What semantic HTML element holds copyright notices and bottom navigation links?
chap-we-09.explanation: <footer> is the semantic element for page closing metadata.

chap-we-09.question_text: What HTTP error code indicates that a link points to a missing or broken page?
chap-we-09.explanation: 404 is the universal status code for a missing page.

chap-we-09.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Connecting Multi-Page Websites works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-09.model_answer: Multi-page websites organize files into structured project folders. index.html acts as the main homepage, connecting to secondary pages via relative links in the navigation bar. Replicating the header and footer across all pages ensures a consistent user experience.
chap-we-09.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Connecting Multi-Page Websites.

chap-we-10.question_text: What is the primary concept taught in Chapter 10: Capstone Website — My Wildlife Reserve?

options.text: The capstone synthesizes semantic HTML structure, responsive CSS styling, card components, and multi-page links into a live animal sanctuary portal
CSS is only for video games
Web development cannot be learned in school

chap-we-10.explanation: The capstone website brings together all structural and visual web development skills.

options.text: A visual layout blueprint sketching headers, content sections, and card grids before writing code
An electric cable inside the monitor

chap-we-10.explanation: Wireframes plan page architecture and visual hierarchy before coding.

chap-we-10.question_text: Why are card components so popular in modern web design?

options.text: They organize related photos, titles, and text into modular, visually appealing containers
They are the only allowed shape

chap-we-10.explanation: Cards bundle modular content into scannable visual units.

chap-we-10.question_text: What are the two core technologies you mastered in Web Explorers?
chap-we-10.explanation: HTML and CSS form the foundational languages of the World Wide Web.

chap-we-10.question_text: What official certificate badge did you earn by completing the Web Explorers curriculum?

options.text: Certified Web Explorer & Junior Web Designer 🌐🏆

chap-we-10.explanation: Graduating certifies complete foundational web literacy and design mastery!

chap-we-10.question_text: Short Answer Assessment: In your own words, summarize how Capstone Website — My Wildlife Reserve works in computer programming and explain why it is essential.
chap-we-10.model_answer: The Wildlife Reserve Capstone unites all web development skills: planning with wireframes, structuring with semantic HTML5 tags (header, nav, section, footer), styling with modern CSS colors, fonts, borders, and the Box Model, and publishing a multi-section sanctuary portal.
chap-we-10.explanation: Review the model answer to verify key concepts of Capstone Website — My Wildlife Reserve.
